channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Proposed 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule: What PTs Need to Know, Part 1
item.description: The U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services estimates a 1-3% overall payment increase for physical therapy codes under the Calendar Year 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule Proposed Rule.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Fake podiatrist sentence to be served in the community
item.description: A fake podiatrist in Australia was sentenced to community service, highlighting the importance of regulatory compliance in healthcare professions.
item.author: AHPRA

item.title: ACCESS for Primary Care Providers and Referring Clinicians
item.description: The CMS Innovation Center launched the ACCESS model, a 10-year pilot offering ongoing, technology-supported chronic care from Medicare-enrolled providers at low or no cost to patients.
item.author: CMS

item.title: Beyond "Biomedical-Plus": Reclaiming the biopsychosocial model in musculoskeletal physiotherapy.
item.description: This article argues that musculoskeletal physiotherapists can move towards a more authentic application of the biopsychosocial (BPS) model by focusing on three interconnected foundational conditions: professional Confidence, role Clarity, and Compassionate communication, to counter the current "biomedical-plus" approach.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of Combined Biopsychosocial Interventions for Chronic Low Back Pain: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated combined biopsychosocial interventions for chronic low back pain, finding them effective in reducing pain and functional disability in adults (≥18 years) compared to usual care, waiting-list controls, and active unimodal interventions.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative efficacy of different joint mobilization techniques in shoulder adhesive capsulitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis compared the clinical effects of different non-thrust joint mobilization approaches on objective and subjective outcomes in individuals with shoulder adhesive capsulitis, based on English-language RCTs published between 2000 and 2025.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: APTA Members Unite to Advance Payment Advocacy Via New SPARC Forum and Pledge
item.description: APTA has launched the SPARC Forum and the APTA Payment Advocacy Pledge to empower members in driving meaningful payment reform and strengthening the future of the physical therapy profession, especially regarding payer advocacy in states.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Dry Needling State Laws
item.description: APTA provides an updated infographic (as of April 2026) detailing state laws on dry needling practice by physical therapists in the US, highlighting which states allow, prohibit, or have no specific provisions.
item.author: APTA

item.title: From mechanics to mobilization: a biomechanically-informed rehabilitation framework for cesarean-related scars | BMC Women's Health
item.description: This systematic review developed a biomechanically-informed rehabilitation framework for cesarean-related scars, integrating superficial and deep scar considerations.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Effectiveness of different modes of digital health interventions for sarcopenia in older adults: a systematic review and network meta-analysis | BMC Geriatrics
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of different modes of digital health interventions for sarcopenia in older adults.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Outpatient rehabilitation can prevent suicide after acquired brain injury.
item.description: A registry study (n=591 treated, n=2,932 controls) supplemented with medical record reviews found that outpatient rehabilitation programs for adults with acquired brain injuries (ABI) were associated with a lower frequency of suicides compared to a matched control group, suggesting a preventive role.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A systematic review of current evidence on clinical outcomes of lumbar roll and modified SIMS manipulation techniques in sacroiliac joint dysfunction.
item.description: This systematic review aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of lumbar roll and modified SIMS manipulation techniques for sacroiliac joint dysfunction (SIJD), searching studies published between January 2021 and December 2025.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exploring equity in telehealth interventions in physiotherapy: A meta-epidemiological study.
item.description: A meta-epidemiological study (n=94 trials) assessed equity in telehealth interventions in physiotherapy research using the PROGRESS Plus framework, finding that most studies did not adequately report or focus on equity factors.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Contralateral Balance Training Improves Postural Control and Functional Recovery After Arthroscopic Anterior Talofibular Ligament Repair: A Prospective, Randomized, Single-Blind Trial | Sports Medicine - Open
item.description: A prospective, randomized, single-blind trial found that contralateral balance training improved postural control and functional recovery after arthroscopic anterior talofibular ligament repair.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Effects of resistance-band shoulder exercise on pain, range of motion, and functional disability in diabetic adults with adhesive capsulitis: a pilot randomized controlled trial | BMC Musculoskeletal Disorders
item.description: A pilot randomized controlled trial found that resistance-band shoulder exercise improved pain, range of motion, and functional disability in diabetic adults with adhesive capsulitis.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Kinesiotaping May Reduce Early Swelling After Knee Replacement, states study
item.description: A study with 136 randomized patients found that adding kinesiotaping to standard rehabilitation after total knee arthroplasty reduced early postoperative knee swelling and produced a modest improvement in knee flexion.
item.author: Medical Dialogues

item.title: Effectiveness of Visual Needle Knife Release in Treating Knee Osteoarthritis: A Meta-analysis | Indian Journal of Orthopaedics
item.description: A meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of visual needle knife release in treating knee osteoarthritis.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Effects of square-step exercise on fear of falling in older patients with ischemic stroke: a cluster randomized controlled trial | BMC Geriatrics
item.description: A cluster randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of square-step exercise on fear of falling, balance, ADLs, and fall risk in older ischemic stroke patients.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: γ-transcranial alternating current stimulation improves upper-limb motor function in stroke patients and modulates oscillatory imbalance: a pilot randomized controlled trial | Journal of NeuroEngineering and Rehabilitation
item.description: A pilot randomized controlled trial found that γ-transcranial alternating current stimulation improved upper-limb motor function in stroke patients and modulated oscillatory imbalance.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Specific mode acupoint electrical stimulation combined with NGF for neurological recovery in ischemic stroke convalescence: A randomized controlled study | BMC Medicine
item.description: A randomized controlled study investigated specific mode acupoint electrical stimulation combined with NGF for neurological recovery in ischemic stroke convalescence.
item.author: Sports Medicine
